scientific_checks.stationary_exponential_domain_proof: For |chi|<=.35 use f=exp(a*v²/2), a=.4-.5*chi. Uniform margins: .225<=a<=.575<.625<=1/Ta and .225<=a+chi<=.575<.7142857<=1/Tb. The marked jump gain divided by f decays quadratically in v with a finite incoming Gaussian integral; OU has negative quadratic leading term, motor flips leave f fixed. A finite uniform upper bound on L_chi f/f and finite stationary E[f] prove the measured exponential moments are finite. No maximal-strip claim is made.

previous_full_domain_and_thermodynamic_e.continuous_domain_moment_argument: For every even p>=2, OU contributes -p*gamma*|v|^p plus a lower-power diffusion term; the positive jump part is at most lambda*(M_p+|v|M_p+M_{p+1}), uniformly in eta in[0,1] and bounded incoming means/temperatures. Young bounds yield L|v|^p<=-c|v|^p+C. Linear event hazard and these moments imply nonexplosion. OU ellipticity and bounded-parameter Gaussian reset irreducibility yield geometric ergodicity and integrable heat cumulants. An analogous exp(a*v²) argument holds for a<1/(2*maxTa,Tb), justifying Gaussian tail control.
